title: Constructibility transfers to prime coefficients through an abelian sheaf isomorphism
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and $\Lambda$ a finite commutative ring. Let $r$ be a prime, $F$ a constructible sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{Et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], [def-constructible-constructible], and $G$ a sheaf of $\operatorname{ULift}(\mathbf Z/r)$-modules on this site. If their underlying abelian sheaves are isomorphic, then $G$ is constructible. No curve, nonempty-scheme or nonzero-ring hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Theorem 03SC, second proof paragraph, passage from prime-annihilated sheaves to constructible prime-field sheaves; Definition 03RW (2),(3). Agent-expanded coefficient bookkeeping.

proof.text: Choose the stratification S supplied by IsConstructibleSheaf.exists_stratification for F. Fix a stratum, and let F′ and G′ be the module pullbacks to it.

The underlying abelian sheaf of F′ is locally constant: use its same LocallyConstantDatum and forget each constant restriction, since constants commute with coefficient forgetting. Its geometric stalks are finite: finite generation over the finite coefficient ring implies finiteness, and Point.sheafFiberCompIso identifies the abelian stalk with the underlying module stalk. This is proved directly in the private helper finiteAbelianLocal_of_module.

For each coefficient ring form asIso of the canonical inverse-image comparison. Its invertibility is isIso_moduleAbelianInverseImageComparison. Compose the inverse comparison for G, the abelian inverse image of e, and the comparison for F to obtain an isomorphism from the underlying abelian sheaf of G′ to that of F′. Transport local constancy by IsLocallyConstantSheaf.of_iso and finite stalks by the equivalence induced by the stalk functor.

Primality gives NeZero r. Apply finite_local_cyclic_module_forget_iff to G′ and the abelian local-constancy and finite-stalk data, obtaining finite constant module values. Apply finite_locally_constant_module_values_iff to conclude IsFiniteLocallyConstantSheaf G′. Repeat for every stratum of S and use the constructor of IsConstructibleSheaf. The empty stratification, empty cover members, and zero sheaf require no additional hypotheses.

proof_origin.place: Theorem 03SC second proof paragraph and Definition 03RW (2),(3); preserve the original stratification, forget finite module stalks, and apply the existing cyclic-coefficient finite-values equivalence.

theorem isConstructibleSheaf_prime_of_underlyingAbelianIso
    (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ] [Finite Λ] (X : Scheme.{u})
    (r : ℕ) [Fact r.Prime]
    (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)) [IsConstructibleSheaf F]
    (G : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod r))))
    (e : (sheafCompose _ (forget₂
          (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod r))) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})).obj G ≅
        (sheafCompose _ (forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})).obj F) :
    IsConstructibleSheaf G
